source.title: Slikovnice, lektire, djetinjstvo... Zašto su priče važnije nego što mislimo? Željka Horvat Vukelja

summary.title_hr: Slikovnice, lektire, djetinjstvo... Zašto su priče važnije nego što mislimo? Željka Horvat Vukelja
summary.abstract_hr: U 53. epizodi podcasta voditeljica Iva Kraljević razgovara sa Željkom Horvat Vukeljom, dječjom književnicom, nekadašnjom učiteljicom francuskog i dugogodišnjom urednicom Modre laste. Razgovor se bavi pričama iz njezina djetinjstva, time mijenjaju li se djeca, zašto je priča prije svega doživljaj, kako prepoznati dobru slikovnicu i jesu li stare bajke prestrašne za djecu. Govori se i o ekranima, audio bajkama, lektirama poput Družbe Pere Kvržice te o važnosti igre i roditeljske prisutnosti. Glavna je poruka da za pričanje priča roditelji ne moraju biti stručni ni posebno maštoviti, nego prisutni, jer je pažnja najljepši dar koji djetetu mogu dati.
key_topics: modra lasta i rad s djecom
key_points: Gošća ističe da je priča prije svega doživljaj: ljudi zaborave imena, brojke i mjesta, ali ne zaborave je li im bilo lijepo ili ružno.

Prema gošći, srž djece se nije promijenila jer su i dalje radoznala, iskrena i zaigrana. Mijenja se kontekst oko njih, pa danas imaju kraću pažnju, a pripovjedač mora biti zanimljiviji i 'mozaičniji'.
Pažnja je najljepši dar i izraz ljubavi prema djetetu. Roditeljima savjetuje da mobitel 'ostave u špajzi' dok su s djetetom, osim u životno važnim situacijama.

Roditelji koji misle da nisu maštoviti mogu pričati priče iz običnog života. Važniji su ton, uživljenost i prisutnost od same radnje, a druga imena ili životinjski likovi pomažu da se dijete ne osjeća izmanipulirano.
Kod starih bajki smatra da smo danas možda 'preanalitični'. Klasično, mirno pričanje bez detalja djecu u pravilu ne plaši, a uz brižljivu pripremu može se ponuditi i drukčiji, sretniji kraj.
Ne zalaže se za zabrane knjiga ni lektira, nego za načelo 'dobrim potisnuti loše'. Roditelji ne trebaju biti čistunci, ali trebaju zaviriti u sadržaje koje djeca čitaju i igraju.

Družbu Pere Kvržice ne bi micala iz lektire jer je Pero poduzetan, hrabar i pun ideja, što je 'vječan lik'. Djecu u starije lektire treba uvesti kroz slike i objašnjenje konteksta, primjerice što je mlin.
key_topics_en: required reading and classics of children's literature
Modra lasta and working with children
key_points_en: The guest emphasizes that a story is above all an experience: people forget names, numbers, and places, but they do not forget whether it was pleasant or unpleasant for them.

According to the guest, the core of children has not changed because they are still curious, sincere, and playful. The context around them is changing, so today they have a shorter attention span, and the storyteller must be more interesting and more 'mosaic-like'.
Attention is the most beautiful gift and expression of love toward a child. She advises parents to 'leave the cell phone in the pantry' while they are with the child, except in vital life situations.

Parents who think they are not imaginative can tell stories from ordinary life. Tone, immersion, and presence are more important than the plot itself, and different names or animal characters help ensure the child does not feel manipulated.

Regarding old fairy tales, she believes that today we are perhaps 'overly analytical'. Classic, calm storytelling without details generally does not frighten children, and with careful preparation, a different, happier ending can also be offered.

She does not advocate for banning books or required reading, but rather for the principle of 'suppressing the bad with the good'. Parents should not be puritans, but they should take a peek into the content that children read and play.

She would not remove Družba Pere Kvržice from required reading because Pero is enterprising, brave, and full of ideas, which is an 'eternal character'. Children should be introduced to older required reading through pictures and an explanation of the context, such as what a mill is.
summary.title_en: Picture Books, Required Reading, Childhood... Why Are Stories More Important Than We Think? Željka Horvat Vukelja
summary.abstract_en: In the 53rd episode of the podcast, host Iva Kraljević talks with Željka Horvat Vukelja, a children's writer, former French teacher, and long-time editor of Modra lasta. The conversation deals with stories from her childhood, whether children are changing, why a story is above all an experience, how to recognize a good picture book, and whether old fairy tales are too scary for children. There is also discussion about screens, audio fairy tales, required reading such as Družba Pere Kvržice, and the importance of play and parental presence. The main message is that to tell stories, parents do not have to be experts or particularly imaginative, but present, because attention is the most beautiful gift they can give to a child.
